D.t: Fred Clark trails by 9.8 and wins 9% of simulations. Closing it takes about 18,373 voters switching sides, or 36,745 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +19.3 and R +0.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
$174K cash against $663K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

R.t: Michael Alfonso leads by 9.8 in the forecast and wins 91% of simulations. The cushion is about 36,745 votes; a one point swing is about 1,881 voters changing sides.
